chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the man who has sheep, he gives them out (for pasture) with a tribute of butter, a known amount, or known dirhams, from every sheep such and such. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with the dirhams, and I do not like it if it is with the butter.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay for sheep grazing in kind (butter) or money (dirhams)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the fiqh of 'ribat al-ganm' (leasing livestock for grazing), where the Imam (AS) validates the permissibility of fixed monetary compensation (dirhams) while expressing a personal preference against using butter (saman) as payment. This distinction highlights the scholarly nuance between strict legal validity (jays) and recommended practice (awla), reflecting the practical economic considerations of the early Shia community regarding commodity valuation and contract clarity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who happens to have the sheep for him, he gives it out (for pasture) with a tribute of butter, something known, or a known amount of Dirhams, from every sheep such and such. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is not problem with the Dirhams, and I<sup>asws</sup> do not like it if it happens to be with the butter’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

About the case of a man who owns sheep and gives them to be maintained and paid for their maintenance from their ghee a certain amount or a known amount of dirham for every sheep, abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Dirham is not unlawful but I do not like giving ghee.’”
